hypotheses.title: 10-Day Linear Smoothed Competitor Lead-Lag Spread
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Direct competitors (pv13 / rel_ret_comp, 82% matrix coverage) share common input costs, customer bases, and macro industry cycles. Due to fragmented order flow, stock prices adjust sequentially rather than instantaneously. In Batch 286, this raw spread achieved Sharpe 1.53 but suffered high 45% turnover. Replacing raw returns with dimensionless return (close - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1) eliminates unit warnings, and smoothing across a 10-day decay window filters high-frequency noise, slashing turnover towards 20-25% to propel Fitness > 1.20.
confounders: Structural market-share losses that justify permanent company underperformance against direct competitors
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if 10-day smoothed spread yields Fitness < 1.00 or turnover > 70% in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 10-day decayed dimensionless spread between direct competitor returns and firm returns.

hypotheses.title: 15-Day Deep Trend Competitor Lead-Lag Spread
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Extending the decay horizon to 15 trading days captures sustained institutional benchmark rebalancing across competing firms. A 15-day linear decay further compresses portfolio turnover into the 15-18% range, providing maximum mathematical leverage to the Fitness multiplier sqrt(Return / Turnover) to achieve Fitness >= 1.40-1.50+ while preserving high Sharpe stability.
confounders: Protracted industry consolidation reducing the effective number of competing firms
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if 15-day smoothed spread fails to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 and Fitness >= 1.00 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 15-day decayed dimensionless spread between competitor returns and firm returns for minimum turnover.

hypotheses.title: 10-Day Cumulative Competitor Return Divergence Spread
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Rather than decaying daily return differences, directly comparing the 10-day cumulative competitor return (ts_sum(rel_ret_comp, 10)) with the firm's 10-day cumulative return ((close - ts_delay(close, 10)) / ts_delay(close, 10)) quantifies structural performance divergence. Smoothing this cumulative divergence with ts_decay_linear(..., 5) isolates genuine analyst benchmark catch-up while maintaining zero unit friction and low turnover.
confounders: Asymmetric earnings announcements where competitors have reported quarterly numbers but the firm has not
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cumulative competitor return divergence yields Fitness < 1.00 or Sharpe < 1.25 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 5-day decay of 10-day cumulative performance divergence between competitors and the firm.
